title: The record's classification drives the transport response's retry hint
asA: caller of an application endpoint that failed
iWant: the transport response to reflect whether the failure is retryable
soThat: my retry policy honours the origin's judgement instead of guessing from the status code alone

acceptanceCriteria.description: A record with category transient produces a wire response the transport ADR maps to a retryable envelope (HTTP: a 5xx or a 429 with a Retry-After hint when the origin supplied one on the record); a record with category permanent produces a non-retryable envelope with no Retry-After (HTTP: a 4xx); a record with category unknown is treated as permanent by the wire but logged at error level.
acceptanceCriteria.given: three failing handler paths that construct records with category transient, permanent and unknown respectively
acceptanceCriteria.then: the transport response bodies and headers reflect the per-class contract above
